newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: ALPINE SKIING-NORWAY'S LOEDEMEL ATTEMPTING COMEBACK.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-NORWAY'S LOEDEMEL ATTEMPTING COMEBACK.

text.p: Norway's Astrid Loedemel,a former world championship medallist, is attempting a comeback to the Alpine ski-racing circuit after a two-year injury break.

Loedemel's first trial on race skis since tearing a cruciate ligament in January 1994 went well on Wednesday when she was a forerunner for an International Ski Federation (FIS) giant slalom race in Flachau, Austria.

The 25-year-old Loedemel, who won downhill silver and super-G bronze at the 1993 world championships in Morioka, Japan, has rejoined the Norwegian ski team this week in Bad Kleinkircheim, where two World Cup downhills and a super-G are scheduled from Friday to Sunday.
Norwegian coaches said that for the moment Loedemel would only train with the team. Whether she would return to competitive racing had not yet been decided.
"She was and is one of our best skiers. We have to give her a second chance," said Norwegian team coach Herbert Sinn.
Loedemel's career came to an abrubt halt when she was injured in a fall during a controversial World Cup race in Altenmarkt in 1994 which was later interrupted due to poor piste conditions.
Numerous operations, a chronic infection and recurring pains in her injured knee prevented Loedemel from rejoining the circuit earlier.
During the two-year break, Loedemel studied French in Paris and worked as a commentator for Norwegian television.
